items.statement: SSG services driving margins upward, improving revenue quality and enabling annuity-led growth
items.quote: The SSG services are helping us to drive the margins upward, which SVK also touched upon that. And along with that, improving the revenue quality and finally, having annuity-led growth for us.

items.statement: AI Exchange platform has 450-plus curated, ready-to-deploy AI agents across multiple industries and business functions
items.quote: Today, I'm proud to share with you that AI Exchange has more than about 450- plus curated, ready to deploy AI agents across multiple different industries, multiple different business functions and, of course, customer personas.

items.statement: Investments predominantly in opex for initial 3 to 5 years to build capability before leveraging for better profitability
items.quote: Investments will be there and predominantly; Information Classification: RL\General Business\Third Party the investments will be in opex. And we think, that would be there for the initial 3 to 5 years. Once we have built the capability, we should be able to leverage from there

items.statement: Launching AI Center of Excellence in Singapore (Launchpad) as regional hub with satellite launch pads in each country
items.quote: Launching the AI center of excellence. And Sayantan has also mentioned, in Singapore, we call it the Launchpad that will serve a regional hub for innovation, software development and partner enablement that will lead the region from a hub point of view.

items.statement: Building deep technical capabilities across cloud, cybersecurity, software, enterprise software and AI as main pain point in SESA region
items.quote: Building the deep technical capabilities across the cloud, cybersecurity, software, enterprise software and AI. That is the one of the main pain points of the region as well, creating the capability and the competencies.

items.statement: Top 6 vendors contribute 70% plus of SSG revenue; focus on adding new categories and brands to improve mix
items.quote: The top 6 vendors contribute about 70% plus of the revenue today. But this is pretty much the trend across the industry. The key here is to continue to add on new categories and new brands in each of these categories.

items.statement: SME transactions 70% vs enterprise 30% by count, but revenue ratio may flip due to large enterprise deal sizes
items.quote: If we look at the number of transaction mix between large enterprise deals and SME deals, it will be very much lopsided towards SME -- number of transactions with SMEs and the number of customers that we deal with to about 70%, 30%.

items.statement: SSG working capital similar to hardware business; lower inventory but longer AR days, higher profitability drives stronger ROCE
items.quote: If you put the math, you will still find the working capital range more or less between our hardware business in SSG. However, because of higher profitability, the return on capital employed is stronger.

items.statement: Capex remains low; investments predominantly in opex for 3-5 years with conscious profit growth management
items.quote: our capex is pretty low. And in this case also, it will continue to be the case. Investments will be there and predominantly; Information Classification: RL\General Business\Third Party the investments will be in opex

items.statement: Professional services at stage 2-3 on scale of 1-10; targeting 8-9 with significant headcount addition and upskilling this year
items.quote: On a scale of 1 to 10, I can say, Information Classification: RL\General Business\Third Party clearly, we are on a stage where we are 2 to 3, and we really need to get to 8 to 9 on a professional

items.statement: Adding significant headcount in professional services this year across practice leads, delivery, pre-sales, solution architects
items.quote: We are identifying where we have gaps. We're actually adding a lot of headcounts this year.

items.statement: Services revenue growing at 100% rate driving transformation-led growth and annuity revenue
items.quote: Services, while growing is 100% rate, but it's not just a revenue add- on when it comes to transformation. It's actually a mechanism which is driving the adoption.

items.statement: Not competing head-on with system integrators; building competency to complement partners and take share based on value added
items.quote: No, we are not. It is a very complex space, as what Sayantan described, whether it is cloud, whether it is security, whether it is AI. And our role is to build co mpetency and certifications inside and bring those capability and certifications and complementarity to our partners

items.statement: Middle East growth driven by national digitalization and compliance mandates
items.quote: The Middle East has a larger enterprise and the government growth that is set behind the national digitalization and the compliance mandate.

items.statement: Vendor consolidation risk mitigated by strong partner designations like Microsoft Frontier partner status
items.quote: If tomorrow, any of these vendors decide to do any consolidation of their partners, we have a better chance to stay on with them. That's a big advantage in an ecosystem like this.

items.statement: AI Exchange platform enables deployment of pre-validated AI agents in weeks rather than months, providing speed as competitive advantage
items.quote: If you as a customer has a particular business need on AI, we can find, configure and deploy pre-validated agents in hardly a couple of weeks. You don't need to really wait for months. You don't need to really build it from the scratch.

items.statement: S-Devices opportunity emerging with NPU-enabled devices and falling inference costs for endpoint AI workloads
items.quote: With proliferation of NPU-enabled devices as well as the way the cost of inferencing is going down, I see a great opportunity for AI workload to move into the endpoint solutions and without worry of what latency, without worrying about the cost of the tokens.

items.statement: Hardware business growing 17% globally vs market degrowth of -2% to -3%; GPU servers and edge PCs exploding
items.quote: Our hardware business has grown at 17%. Globally, the hardware business is actually a degrowth. If you look at the total distribution marketplace, it is a minus 2% to 3% degrowth.

items.statement: Trial production to start in Q4 FY27, commercial production in Q1 FY28
items.quote: On the time line, we expect trial production to commence in quarter 4 of FY '27, with commercial production to start by quarter 1 of FY '28.

items.statement: Year 1 volume target of 8-9 million units, year 2 target of 13-15 million units
items.quote: On the scale side, we expect to begin with around 8 million units in year 1, followed by a calibrated phase-wise ramp-up. If everything goes as scheduled, we expect to touch the volumes of around 13 million to 15 million in second year of operations.

items.statement: Initial capex below INR 50 crore for assembly and SMT; component capex later
items.quote: To start with on the assembly and SMT, we are not putting in any capex. It will be minimum. It will be below INR50 crores to start with.

items.statement: Subleasing existing Oppo facility with dedicated lines; no new capacity build initially
items.quote: Facility side, the manufacturing will be carried out at an existing facility under an sublease arrangement with Oppo India.

items.statement: Initial EBITDA margins 1.5-2% (ex-PLI), improving with scale and local value addition
items.quote: If we consider minus the PLI part of it, normally, the industry is operating at 1.5% to 2% of EBITDA levels, depending on which model do you make.

items.statement: Standalone ROCE expected >30-35%; component business at 15-16% margins
items.quote: If you take this on a stand-alone basis, I mean, the ROCEs will be more than 30%, 35%.

items.statement: Net working capital days of 4-5 days, maximum 10 days
items.quote: Normally, this sector operates on a net-working capital days of almost 4, 5 days, maximum 10 days.

items.statement: Starting with assembly and SMT; adding HDI PCBs in year 2, targeting 30-35% local value addition in 5-6 years
items.quote: We'll start with assembly and SMT and in year 1 -- year 2, sorry, not year 1 -- year 2, we will be adding our HDI whenever HDI plans will be ready. That is our first foray. An d then we can take this local value addition to 35% to 40% in the next 5 to 6 years

items.statement: Covers Oppo, OnePlus, Realme (BBK Group); no arrangement with Vivo currently
items.quote: On the scope, this agreement covers 3 brands, which is Oppo, OnePlus and Realme.

items.statement: No Press Note 3 approval required for sublease structure
items.quote: This structure does not require any Press Note 3 approval.

items.statement: Dedicated senior management for mobile division; PCB division headed by Mr. Santosh (25 years experience, ex-AT&S)
items.quote: Certainly, it requires a very dedicated efforts. And certainly, there will be a senior most management dedicated to this sector only.

items.statement: Ascent PCB division now headed by Mr. Santosh after Mr. Manjunath stepped down
items.quote: But on the heading side, it will be headed the whole division, PCB division will be headed by Mr. Santosh. He has 25 years experience in the printed circuit board category. He was earlier heading AT&S.

items.statement: Industry local value addition currently 10-12%; Amber targets 35-40% in 5-6 years
items.quote: But what we see as Amber is on the local value addition. So we have just -- the industry is at just 10%, 12% of local value addition right now.

items.statement: Not disrupting Oppo's existing EMS relationships; may supply components to them later
items.quote: See, we have requested them not to give others business to us. That is not Amber's model. So, I believe it will get -- it will continue in the shape and form, which is happening right now.

items.statement: No fund raise mentioned; minimal capex funded internally
items.quote: On the capital outlay, consistent with the asset-light nature of this collaboration, capex requirements are very, very minimal.

items.statement: PLI scheme structure uncertain; waiting for draft notification before commenting on backward integration focus
items.quote: Well, it's very early statement to make right now because we don't have even the draft of the second PLI, which is being talked about.

items.statement: Targeting revenue growth of approximately 30% to 35% in FY27 while maintaining focus on profitability and capital efficiency
items.quote: Based on our current business momentum and growth initiative, we are targeting revenue growth of approximately 30% to 35% of FY27, while maintaining a strong focus on profitability and also capital efficiency.

items.statement: Expect reagent revenue to grow 30% to 35% in FY27
items.quote: So, last year our reagents revenue grew by 35%. So, we are expecting a 30% to 35% increase in the reagent revenue current year also.

items.statement: No major capex expected for next two years; CWIP of ~INR15 crores for a facility planned as warehouse
items.quote: So we might be using that kind of a facility as a warehouse for now. But yes, however depending upon how our CDMO business kind of grows. So, if we were to get, y ou know, CDMO opportunities for large equipment, then we might need additional space and depending upon that we will develop that facility. Yes, but for now we don't see any major capex

items.statement: Unit 4 facility can support 3x to 4x current revenue in reagent and CDMO business; expect 25-30% utilization in FY27
items.quote: And we expect that about by the end of this year, we will be able to utilize about 25% to you k now 30% of the capacity that we have in Unit 4

items.statement: Existing facility can do 3x to 4x business without additional capital; reagent production could scale 6x to 7x in 2-3 years
items.quote: So, our facility we believe without addition without adding any a dditional capital, so what the business we are doing it, maybe at least 3x to 4x business we can do with the same facility

items.statement: Selectra Pro M installation base crossed 1,550 units; added 450+ units in FY26
items.quote: Our Selectra Pro M fully automated biochemistry analyzer, which entered commercially commercial production only a little over two years ago, has now it crossed the installation base is more than 1,550 instruments.

items.statement: Total installed base of 16,000-17,000 instruments across all categories; plan to add ~2,000 instruments in FY27
items.quote: Overall till date, Ajay sir can also add in, we will have a base of some 17,000 instruments. So, since the inc eption, when Q-Line has started doing business, so earlier we were trading, we were importing instruments a nd placing them. Now, we have also started manufacturing. So, as of now we will have a total base of 16,000 to 17,000 instruments till date. And this year also, we just discussed ab

items.statement: Gross margin expanded from 53.3% to 60.8% in FY26; EBITDA margin improved from 22.5% to 28.7%
items.quote: Gross margin expanded significantly from 53.3% in FY25 to 60.8% in FY26, an improvement of approximately 750 basis points.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins to remain slightly better than FY26 due to 35-40% reagent revenue growth from manufactured products
items.quote: And the EBITDA margins will continue as we've seen in the last financial year because as we spoke that we are expecting a large reagent revenue. And when we look at the reagents, especially the manufactured reagents, our margins are about 60% to 65%. And overall when we look it at the big picture where we also include the traded product and instrument segments, so we expect the EBITDA margins to k

items.statement: Reagents contribute ~70% of revenue; manufactured reagents 70% of reagent revenue, traded 30%
items.quote: Looking at the business mix, reagents continue to be the primary g rowth driver and accounted for nearly 70% of our total

items.statement: Manufactured reagents grew ~70% in FY26; now 70% of reagent sales are in-house
items.quote: During the year, sales of manufactured reagents increased nearly 70%, validating our strategy of increasing in-house production and value addition.

items.statement: 65% B2G revenue, 35% trade; UP concentration due to billing through promoter distributor who supplies to multiple states
items.quote: Yes. So, about 65% is B2G and 35% is trade. And so we kind of do business through our distributors. So, one of our large distributor is kind of based in UP and so we end up billing, everything to that distributor and hence the concentration shows typ ically in the state of UP

items.statement: Target 50-50 B2G vs trade mix by end of FY28 through exports, CDMO, and new products
items.quote: So, going forward we probably see that this concentration between B2G and others should look around by the end of 28 we should be 50-50 as of now.

items.statement: Export revenue INR1.2 crores in FY26; targeting >5x growth in FY27 excluding CDMO; CDMO expected ~INR10 crores in FY27
items.quote: So, around INR10 crores. So, I'll just add on here, so the exports that we are mentioning are not 5x projection that we are given does not include the CDMO busine ss. So, that is purely the exports where we will be exporting to other countries like Mauritius, S outh Africa or African places, whereas CDMO we expect, we are in the negotiation stage right currently and we expect some traction over he

items.statement: Target working capital ~100 days; receivable days to improve to 90-120 days from current 120-150
items.quote: So, going forward we expect to maintain the receivable cycle within 90 to 120 days. So, up to 120 days. So, that is it.

items.statement: Corporate guarantees for related parties being wound down; no new guarantees planned; IPO proceeds used for debt repayment
items.quote: And in future in any case as part of our IPO proceeds also we're also k ind of repaying a lot of debt at Q-Line also. So, corporate guarantees we expect them to be very minimal for Q-Line as is on its own and also for any other, related party or that we will no t be giving any corporate guarantees in future

items.statement: Per analyzer reagent consumption ~INR25,000-30,000/month; lifetime value ~INR30 lakhs over 8-10 years
items.quote: So, one instrument life is almost 8 to 10 years we are expecting and this is the life of the instrument. So, last year also we have received the additional business aroun d INR20 crores to INR25 crores and after this installation definitely we are expecting similar

items.statement: Hematology reagent business growing 50-55%; sickle cell and malaria screening programs driving open-system reagent growth
items.quote: And our focus is on that also Hematology and successfully we are growing by more than 50% to 55% in reagent business at this moment and highly potential business for us.

items.statement: Sickle cell product received CDSCO license; awarded malaria screening program nationally; qualified for public tenders requiring 3-year market standing
items.quote: Our sickle cell product also we have received the license from the CDSCO at this moment for the you can say global screening program we can participate. Also recently also we participate. we got the award from the malaria screening program in all over India.

items.statement: R&D spend ~INR2.5-3 crores annually; DSIR-approved R&D center; collaborations with IITs and National Institute of Immunology
items.quote: But I mean around INR5 crores, but every year we are spending more than you can say INR2.5 crores to INR3 crores on R&D.

items.statement: Revenue concentration in UP due to promoter distributor; instrument revenue cyclical due to seeding nature
items.quote: So, the seeding of instrument is at times cyclic in nature. So, there has been a slight kind of a dip in the instrument revenue as we compare from FY25 to FY26.

items.statement: Microlab 300 launch expected in FY27; multiple analyzer platforms under development; electrolyte analyzer commercialized in FY26
items.quote: We expect a launch of Microlab 300 during FY27 and continue advancing multiple analyzer platform currently under development.
